help.fullScreen: Shows the game in exclusive full screen instead of a window.
help.borderless: Shows the game in a window without frame or title bar, sized to the screen.
help.resolutionWidth: Width, in pixels, of the image the game renders.
help.resolutionHeight: Height, in pixels, of the image the game renders.
help.vsync: Locks frames to the screen's refresh rate: prevents tearing, but can cap the frame rate.
help.multisample: Smooths object edges by sampling several points per pixel; higher values cost more.
help.transparencyMultisample: Also smooths transparent parts (foliage, fences). Only works with multisampling.
help.fxaa: Fast edge smoothing applied to the final image. Cheap, but makes the picture slightly soft.
help.taa: Temporal anti-aliasing: blends successive frames for clean, stable edges.
help.taaSharpen: Sharpens the image after temporal anti-aliasing.
help.anisotropy: Keeps textures sharp on surfaces seen at a slant (ground, roads). Cheap.
help.gamma: Brightens or darkens the whole image. 1.0 is neutral.
help.screenSpaceReflections: Adds reflections on shiny surfaces based on what is visible on screen.
help.ambientOcclusion: Slightly darkens crevices and corners to give scenes depth.
help.hdr64: Computes lighting with more precision, which reduces banding in gradients. Uses more memory.
help.projectedUV: Projects snow and some surface details onto objects for a more realistic look.
help.parallaxOcclusion: Gives compatible textures (stone, cobbles) depth depending on the viewing angle.
help.precipitationOcclusion: Stops rain and snow from falling under roofs and shelters.
help.lockFramerate: Caps the game at the screen's refresh rate. The game is designed to run at 60 frames per second.
help.fpsClamp: Frame rate ceiling imposed on the game. 0 leaves the game unrestricted.
help.worldFov: The camera's viewing angle, in degrees. Wider shows more at the sides, with stretched edges.
help.shadowResolution: Detail of cast shadows. Higher means sharper and more expensive shadows.
help.shadowDistance: How far, in game units, shadows are computed outdoors.
help.interiorShadowDistance: How far shadows are computed inside enclosed places.
help.focusShadows: Number of extra, highly detailed shadows computed around the character and nearby objects.
help.shadowMaskQuarter: Precision of the mask that applies shadows to the scene. A lower value is finer and costs more.
help.actorSelfShadowing: Characters cast shadows on themselves (folds, hoods, arms).
help.treeShadows: Trees receive shadows from other objects.
help.sunShadowUpdate: Delay, in seconds, between sun shadow updates. Longer costs less.
help.objectFade: Distance at which objects (houses, rocks, ramparts) fade out. Higher means farther.
help.itemFade: Distance at which small items (weapons, books, ingredients) fade out.
help.actorFade: Distance at which characters and creatures fade out.
help.skyCellFade: Draw distance for objects in aerial areas (such as Sovngarde).
help.treeLodSwitch: Distance beyond which trees switch to their simplified version.
help.meshLod1: Distance at which models switch to their first reduced detail level.
help.meshLod2: Distance at which models switch to their second reduced detail level.
help.meshLod1Tree: Distance of the first reduced detail level, for trees.
help.meshLod2Tree: Distance of the second reduced detail level, for trees.
help.meshFadePercent: Share of the distance used to blend one detail level into the next.
help.lightFade: Distance at which lights start to fade.
help.lightFadeRange: Length over which lights fade until they disappear.
help.autoViewDistance: The game adjusts the view distance by itself to hold the frame rate.
help.autoViewMin: Distance the automatic adjustment never goes below.
help.grassFade: Distance at which grass starts to fade.
help.grassFadeMin: Smallest fade start distance grass can get.
help.grassFadeMax: Largest fade start distance grass can get.
help.grassMinSize: Size of the generated grass patches: the smaller, the denser the grass.
help.grassDraw: Shows the grass generated by the game.
help.grassPointLighting: Grass is lit by point lights (torches, fires), not only by the sun.
help.terrainBlock0: Distance up to which the terrain is shown at full detail.
help.terrainBlock1: Distance up to which the terrain is shown at intermediate detail.
help.terrainMax: Distance beyond which distant terrain is no longer shown.
help.terrainSplit: Multiplier for the distance at which terrain blocks are subdivided.
help.treeLoadDistance: Distance up to which distant trees are loaded.
help.largeRefGrid: Size of the grid of simplified distant objects (mountains, forts). Wider shows farther.
help.treesEnabled: Shows trees. Off, the world has no trees.
help.skinnedTrees: Nearby trees use models that bend in the wind.
help.skinnedTreeCount: Maximum number of skinned trees shown at once.
help.waterReflections: Water reflects the sky and surroundings.
help.waterRefractions: Distorts what you see through water.
help.waterDisplacements: Water reacts to movement (steps, projectiles) with ripples.
help.waterDepth: Water colour and transparency vary with its depth.
help.waterSilhouettes: Water also reflects the silhouettes of nearby objects and characters.
help.volumetricLighting: Light rays visible in the air (mist, dust, sunbeams).
help.volumetricQuality: Detail of volumetric lighting. Higher costs more.
help.improvedSnow: Snow with a more realistic look (depth, shine).
help.sunbeams: Sun rays visible through clouds and foliage.
help.depthOfField: Blurs what is far or near the thing you look at, in dialogue and menus.
help.lensFlare: Light halos when looking toward the sun.
help.radialBlur: Blur around the image during some effects (spells, hits).
help.decals: Blood splatter, scorch marks and impacts that stay on surfaces.
help.skinnedDecals: Decals also appear on characters and creatures.
help.maxDecals: Maximum number of decals kept on surfaces.
help.maxSkinDecals: Maximum number of decals kept on characters.
help.maxDecalsPerFrame: Maximum number of decals created each frame.
help.maxSkinDecalsPerFrame: Maximum number of character decals created each frame.
help.maxParticles: Desired number of particles on screen (flames, magic, dust).
help.compass: Shows the compass at the top of the screen.
help.crosshair: Shows the aiming dot at the centre of the screen.
help.hudOpacity: Transparency of in-game interface elements. 1 is opaque, 0 invisible.
help.generalSubtitles: Shows subtitles for ambient conversations and characters.
help.dialogueSubtitles: Shows subtitles during conversations with characters.
help.tutorials: Shows the tips and tutorials that pop up as you play.
help.hudMessages: Shows short messages at the top left (item picked up, quest updated).
help.enemyHealthTime: How long, in seconds, an enemy's health bar stays visible after you hit it.
help.subtitleDistance: Maximum distance at which a character's subtitles are shown.
help.difficulty: The game's difficulty level: the higher it is, the tougher enemies are and the more damage you take.
help.questMarkers: Shows quest markers on the compass and the map.
help.floatingQuestMarkers: Also shows quest markers in the world, above targets.
help.healthBar: Keeps the character's health bar on screen at all times.
help.language: Language of the game's text and voices. The files for that language must be installed.
help.alwaysRun: The character runs by default instead of walking.
help.invertY: Reverses camera movement up and down.
help.mouseSensitivity: Camera turning speed with the mouse.
help.gamepadSensitivity: Camera turning speed with the controller.
help.saveOnPause: Saves automatically when you open the pause menu.
help.saveOnRest: Saves automatically when you sleep or rest.
help.autosaveMinutes: Time, in minutes, between two autosaves.
help.autosaveCount: Number of autosaves kept before the oldest is overwritten.
help.saveBackups: Number of backup copies kept for each save.
help.papyrusLogging: Writes script messages to log files. Useful for troubleshooting, off otherwise.
help.papyrusTrace: Adds detailed traces to the Papyrus log.
help.papyrusProfiling: Measures the time scripts take and writes it to the log.
help.papyrusBudget: Maximum time, in milliseconds, given to scripts each frame.
help.papyrusTaskletBudget: Extra time, in milliseconds, for waiting script tasks.
help.papyrusMemory: Maximum memory, in bytes, scripts can use.
help.zoomIncrement: How far the camera moves with each wheel notch.
help.zoomSpeed: Speed of the camera when zooming.
help.switchDelay: Time, in seconds, before switching between first and third person.
help.shoulderX: Sideways offset of the third-person camera. Negative left, positive right.
help.shoulderZ: Height offset of the third-person camera.
help.shoulderCombatX: Sideways offset of the third-person camera during combat.
help.shoulderCombatZ: Height offset of the third-person camera during combat.
help.shoulderHorseX: Sideways offset of the third-person camera on horseback.
help.shoulderHorseZ: Height offset of the third-person camera on horseback.
help.disableAutoVanity: Stops the camera from orbiting the character on its own when you leave the controls alone.
help.autoVanityDelay: Idle time, in seconds, before the camera starts orbiting on its own.
help.vanityMaxDist: Farthest distance of the camera orbiting the character.
help.vanityMinDist: Closest distance of the camera orbiting the character.
help.masterVolume: Volume of all game sounds. 1 is the maximum.
help.audioEnabled: Turns the game's sound on. Off, the game is silent.
help.musicDucking: Time, in seconds, the music takes to lower when someone speaks.
help.musicUnducking: Time, in seconds, the music takes to come back up after a line of speech.
help.audioCache: Keeps recent sounds in memory to replay them without reloading.
macNote.fullScreen: Under CrossOver, a borderless window is usually more reliable than exclusive full screen.
macNote.borderless: With the screen's resolution, it looks close to full screen without changing the Mac's display mode.
macNote.resolutionWidth: On a Retina display, enter the resolution the game should render, not macOS's point resolution: the higher it is, the harder the graphics chip works.
macNote.resolutionHeight: On a Retina display, enter the resolution the game should render, not macOS's point resolution: the higher it is, the harder the graphics chip works.
macNote.vsync: On a Mac, leave vertical sync on unless your measurements show it does better without: it locks frames to the screen's rhythm.
macNote.multisample: Multisampling is heavy on Apple chips' shared memory: TAA is usually the better choice.
macNote.screenSpaceReflections: Costly on Apple chips: turn it off first if the frame rate is too low.
macNote.ambientOcclusion: Costly on Apple chips: turn it off if the frame rate is too low.
macNote.hdr64: Doubles the memory of HDR targets: avoid it if unified memory is tight.
macNote.lockFramerate: This setting works together with vertical sync: change them one at a time to measure each effect.
macNote.shadowResolution: Shadows are among the costliest settings on a Mac: 2048 is a good starting point, 4096 and above call for a recent chip.
macNote.shadowDistance: The farther the distance, the more shadows the graphics chip computes: lower it before the resolution.
macNote.objectFade: A high value keeps distant objects on screen and puts load on the graphics chip and unified memory.
macNote.grassFade: Distant grass is heavy on an Apple chip: lowering this distance often brings back frames per second.
macNote.terrainBlock0: A large distance loads more detailed terrain and takes more unified memory.
macNote.largeRefGrid: A wider grid loads more distant objects: keep an eye on unified memory.
macNote.waterReflections: Reflections redraw part of the scene: costly on Apple chips.
macNote.volumetricLighting: Volumetric lighting is costly: it is one of the first settings to turn off to gain frames per second.
macNote.volumetricQuality: High levels weigh mostly at high resolutions.
ui.title: Settings editor
ui.intro: Change Skyrim SE's settings without opening a file. Nothing is written without your confirmation, and every save can be undone.
ui.noGame: Skyrim SE was not found. Pick it from the game list.
ui.loadError: Couldn't read the INI files. Check that the bottle is reachable.
ui.presetHint: Fills in the settings they cover without writing anything: you can then adjust them.
ui.notSet: Not set: the game uses its built-in value
ui.confirmIntro: These files will be edited line by line; nothing else changes. A copy is kept before writing and you will be able to undo.
ui.gameRunning: The game or a tool is running. Close it before saving: the game rewrites its INI files on exit and would erase your changes.
ui.readOnly: {{file}} is read-only. Make it writable in the Finder (Get Info), then try again. Nothing was written.
ui.advSearch: Search a setting, a section or a value
ui.advOnlyDefined: Only those defined in my INI files
ui.advEditHint: Double-click a value to edit it. Enter confirms, Esc cancels.
ui.advUnknown: Name unknown to the executable: editable as text
ui.bkIntro: A copy of the INI files is kept before every save. Restoring puts the files back as they were in the copy; the current state is copied first, so you can undo.
ui.bkRestoreBody: The files {{files}} will go back to their state in the backup “{{name}}”. The current state is copied first: you will be able to undo.
ui.ctlIntro: Change Skyrim's keyboard keys: click a key, then press the new one. These are physical key positions, as in the game: ⌘ Command is the game's Windows key.
ui.ctlCustomNew: Your choices will be written to ControlMap_Custom.txt, which does not exist yet.
ui.ctlFindPress: Press the key to look for…
ui.ctlBlocked: A key is used by two actions: fix it before saving.
ui.ctlLoadError: The control table could not be read: {{error}}
ui.ctlConfirmIntro: A copy of the control table with these keys will be written to ControlMap_Custom.txt. The previous version is kept first, so you can undo. The game applies the keys the next time it starts.
